stages.reference: Create a close material reference for smoke-brown stained glass from an old utilitarian building. Its amber-umber pigment should feel mineral and somewhat earthy, passing a low warm light through imperfect but coherent glass. Gentle variations in thickness produce quiet honey-dark and shadow-brown transitions, with only a few subtle cooling marks to reveal the hand of the maker. Keep the material clearly glass, not resin, wood or varnish. Soft light and restrained saturation suit a weathered dark-fantasy settlement better than sparkling luxury. Avoid orange neon, window scenes, dark wooden grain, decorative swirls, hard-edged reflections, thick dirt layers or opaque brown paint. Establish the steady body color that the separate brown detail layer will share.
